description: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy (%) of a misinformation detection model across two datasets — PHEME (left) and PolitiFact (right) — under six different ablation conditions: “Ours” (the full model), “w/o comments,” “w/o text,” “w/o select,” “w/o emotion,” and “w/o cognition.” The vertical axis represents accuracy percentage, ranging from 75.0% to 95.0% in increments of 0.5%, with horizontal gridlines for reference. In the PHEME dataset, the “Ours” model achieves the highest accuracy at 89.84%, followed by “w/o select” at 88.80%, “w/o emotion” at 87.34%, “w/o cognition” at 87.17%, “w/o comments” at 86.82%, and “w/o text” at 80.10%. In the PolitiFact dataset, “Ours” again performs best at 90.57%, followed by “w/o select” at 89.62%, “w/o cognition” at 87.74%, “w/o emotion” at 84.91%, “w/o comments” at 85.85%, and “w/o text” at 83.02%. Each bar is color-coded: “Ours” is dark red, “w/o comments” is orange, “w/o text” is yellow, “w/o select” is light blue, “w/o emotion” is medium blue, and “w/o cognition” is dark blue. The chart visually emphasizes the performance drop when key components (especially text and selection mechanisms) are removed, highlighting their importance in the model’s effectiveness across both datasets.
